sections.archive-one-beliefs: 02 The Practice I have tried plenty of things over the years, without needing each one to become a talent, a hobby or something worth showing anyone. I’m usually more interested in finding out what it’s like, what I can learn from it, and whether I want it to remain part of my life. Sometimes the answer is no, and that is useful to know too. Some things hold my interest and become part of my routine. Others lose their appeal once I understand them a little better. A few leave me with something to take away, even though I never became particularly good at them. I still enjoy trying things without deciding in advance what they need to become. Not every interest has to lead somewhere, and I’m happy to leave room for the next one.
sections.archive-one-things-i-do: 03 Open Tabs Ask what I’m into and I’ll probably give you a list that doesn’t follow much of a pattern: games, music, animals, technology, good conversations and whatever catches my attention online. Each has interested me for a different reason, and I like giving those interests enough time to see where they lead. Some stay with me, while others last only as long as my curiosity does. An interest doesn't have to become a lasting part of my life to have been worth exploring. The list keeps changing, and I’d rather let it do that than try to fit everything into a neat description of myself.
sections.archive-one-favourites: 04 The Usual BLUE Probably my favourite colour, and one I’ve liked for as long as I can remember. My tastes have changed in other ways, but whenever I get to choose, I still come back to it. MILK & WATER My usual drinks. Nothing particularly interesting about that. I like them, and I keep choosing them. MUSIC Kendrick is one of my favourites, though my listening goes well beyond him. My taste moves between genres, artists and sounds, often depending on what I feel like hearing at the time. Some songs stay in rotation; others become attached to a person, a place or a particular period in life. GAMES Volleyball, Football, Cricket, Badminton, Free Fire, Roblox, Chess.com. I’ve spent time with all of them over the years, though not every game or phase lasted. Looking back, I remember fewer scores than the people I played with, the laughter and the long nights that came with it. ANIMALS I like pretty much every animal, but the ones I know best are the dogs and bunnies at home. They become part of everyday life so naturally that you hardly notice it happening. Before long, home would feel different without them.
sections.archive-one-people: 05 By Chance Some of the people I met through games became friends. Others I met in real life, in different places and under different circumstances. Those friendships are all different, and there isn’t one simple explanation for why each came to matter. None of them were planned. Any of those connections could easily have never happened. It's strange to think how many people we might have known if circumstances had been just a little different. I'm glad these particular connections happened.
sections.archive-two-little-things: 06 Not Much to Explain Not everything about me needs a full explanation. A lot of what makes a day better is ordinary: a good conversation, an unexpected laugh, staying up late to play, or finding something new and following it for a while. Music, people I care about, and a few familiar things that feel like mine. I tend to prefer the uncomplicated version of things. Not everything needs to mean something more than it does. Sometimes enjoying it is enough.
sections.archive-two-figuring-out: 07 Some Days I don’t have everything figured out. There are things I believed not long ago that I would answer differently now, and things about myself I still don’t fully understand. There are also parts of my life I know I want to improve, even if I haven’t worked out exactly how yet. Some days I have a fairly clear idea of where I’m headed. Other days, I really don’t. I’m still working out who I’m becoming, and I think it’s fine not to have the whole story yet.
sections.archive-two-things-i-like: 08 Only Later Some moments don’t seem important while they’re happening. They’re ordinary days: passing conversations, late nights, stupid jokes, games with people I happened to meet, and small things I never expected to miss. Only afterwards do they begin to look like they mattered. Not everyone from those days stayed. Some did, some left, and some I had to leave behind. Others were part of my life for a while, taught me something I needed to learn, and eventually became memories. Not every memory is a happy one. There were difficult days, mistakes and moments I wish had gone differently. They belong to the same past as the good ones, even if I remember them differently. What I’m left with are memories of people, places and moments that once meant something. Some still feel close; others have grown distant. I wouldn’t want to erase any of it.
sections.archive-two-memories: 09 Better Questions When someone tells me something, I’d rather understand why it’s true than accept it simply because someone said so. I’m not trying to disagree for the sake of it. Often, I look into things and end up agreeing. I just want the reason behind an opinion to be one I understand, rather than something I’ve accepted without thinking. What interests me most is how people think: how they arrive at what they believe, what shapes those beliefs, and why things work the way they do. I like ideas that stay with me long enough to make me pause what I’m doing and think them through again. I don’t think being smart means knowing everything. To me, it matters more to recognise the limits of what I understand than to pretend they aren’t there. That’s often where the better questions begin.
